name: GlassPerformanceOptimization

tests.nature: templated smoke/axe/className/snapshot plus generic reduced-motion style check; no behavioral assertions on tier switching

material_impl: Shared createGlassStyle({intent:'neutral',elevation:'level2'}) everywhere. The 'adaptive' styles are fake: getOptimizedGlassStyles computes backdropBlur/shadow per mode and then discards them, returning the same createGlassStyle call (193-213); BatteryAwareGlass has three identical branches (408-421); ProgressiveGlassEnhancement enhanced===premium (470-471). Placeholders use hard-coded 12px radius/100px heights (225, 295-296, 427). Imports a CSS file whose only content is a global '@keyframes shimmer' (GlassPerformanceOptimization.css:3-6), and that name can collide with other keyframes.
motion: framer-motion. Reduced motion comes from framer useReducedMotion (52) and is respected in ReducedMotionGlass (348-375). LazyGlassLoading, BatteryAwareGlass (layout), PerformanceMonitor slide-in and ProgressiveGlassEnhancement (layout) ignore it. The default placeholder runs an infinite inline 'shimmer 1.5s infinite' (294) with no reduced-motion guard.
a11y: Purely presentational divs. GlassPerformanceMonitor is fixed top-right at z-max (568-570) with no role/label and can cover app UI. Lazy placeholder has no aria-busy. No focus concerns because nothing is interactive.
api: No forwardRef on any export. EfficientGlassRendering accepts a style prop and ignores it (176, 238). enableGPU and virtualizeContent semantics do nothing visible. VirtualizedContent hard-codes 100px item heights and a 400px container (521, 543). useGlassPerformance throws outside the provider, so every sub-component needs the provider; LazyGlassLoading does not need it, which is inconsistent.
ssr: 'use client'. performance.now() inside effects only, so it is SSR-safe. navigator.getBattery is a deprecated, Chromium-only API.
fake_complexity: High. 'CPU load' is just 100 minus fps/60 (84-85). The perpetual rAF loop is never cancelled because only the first frame id is stored (92-96), so it leaks and calls setState every second forever. Battery listeners' cleanup is returned from inside the promise, so they are never removed (63-69). Mode changes produce no visual difference.
screenshot_review: Image rendering was unavailable to this agent (Read returned empty for PNG/JPEG), so the review used pixel statistics. Desktop: mean RGB 242, channel std 20, saturation 0. A near-white, fully desaturated scene of the summary card and a 2x2 demo grid. There are no depth cues or color identity, and nothing reads above 'grey card on white'.
target: Single headless quality-tier system in core (useGlassQualityTier + CSS custom-property tiers, @media prefers-reduced-transparency/reduced-motion), merged with GlassProgressiveEnhancement and hooks/useGlassOptimization
justification: Eight public exports that look like a performance framework but switch nothing: every tier returns the same createGlassStyle output, and the 'CPU' metric is an fps proxy driven by an uncancelled rAF loop that itself costs performance. Adaptive degradation is a real need for a glass system, but it belongs in one token/CSS-level tier mechanism, not in wrapper components with leaks. Replace with a core tier hook, then deprecate these exports with aliases for one major version.

name: GlassPredictiveEngine
material_impl: Utility classes glass-surface-primary/secondary/subtle, glass-elev-3/4 (976-978, 1010-1011, 1247-1248). It also mixes in un-prefixed Tailwind ('fixed top-4 right-4 z-50', 'w-12 h-12', 'absolute top-14 right-0 w-80 max-h-96') (973, 977, 1010), which the library ships no Tailwind config for, plus a runtime-interpolated arbitrary class `duration-[${ANIMATION.DURATION.normal}ms]` (979) that no JIT can ever generate.
motion: framer-motion with the repo useReducedMotion hook, wired incorrectly. When reduced motion is on, animate={} while initial={{opacity:0}}, so the prediction panel and every list row stay at opacity 0, i.e. invisible (1013-1014, 1044-1045, 1089). 'animate-pulse' on the trigger (980) is not gated.
a11y: The trigger is an icon-only emoji '🧠' button with no aria-label or aria-expanded (975-987). The close button is a bare '✕' with no aria-label (1026-1031). The panel has no dialog/region role, no Escape handling and no focus management. The count badge is a 12px circle holding text (990), which cannot be legible.
api: No forwardRef. The context default is non-null, so the 'must be used within provider' throw is dead code (847-857, 945-953). predictiveEnginePresets are exported but never consumed (1209-1230). The prediction indicator is hard-positioned fixed top-right.
ssr: 'use client'. localStorage access is inside a constructor invoked from useEffect, so it is safe. Interaction data, including click coordinates and modifier keys, is persisted to localStorage under 'auraglass-predictive-data' without consent (284-295, 1147-1152), which is a privacy concern for a UI library.
fake_complexity: Severe. The 'neural network' has randomly initialised weights (186-206) and never learns usefully: train() updates output weights without the hidden activations or inputs (246-251). Neural predictions are therefore random per page load. 'AI insights' are three hard-coded thresholds (568-610). generateWorkflowSuggestions/analyzeBoardPerformance return canned strings with fallback ids 'high-activity-card'/'optimized-flow' (757-799).
screenshot_review: Pixel stats only (image viewer unavailable). Desktop: mean 244, std 13, saturation 0, and the content bbox starts at y=321. A single small grey summary card centred on white ('Monitoring behavior', 'Predictions 0', 'Insights 0'). The story hides the indicator, so the only visual is an empty-state card. Not premium.
justification: Marketed as an AI engine but it is a random-weight perceptron with broken training, threshold-based 'insights', and silent localStorage behavioural logging. Its only UI is an emoji FAB whose panel becomes invisible under reduced motion. A design system should not ship this; if predictive prefetch is wanted, it belongs in an app-level analytics package, not in aura-glass.

name: GlassProgressiveEnhancement
sub_exports: qualityTiers (none root-exported; reachable only via deep import/stories)

tests.nature: templated plus 2 real ones: body tier class and rAF cancel on unmount

material_impl: EnhancedGlass applies a literal codemod artifact as a className: 'OptimizedGlass intensity={0.2} glassBlur={6}' (770). The 'glass' therefore comes only from the story's glass-foundation-complete class. --glass-effective-blur is set (786) but nothing consumes it. Tier definitions carry leftover '// Use createGlassStyle() instead' comments (100, 122, 144, 166, 188).
motion: EnhancedGlass runs an infinite scale [1,1.01,1] 'breathing' loop (775-782) gated by tier and reduced motion (761-762). Reduced motion is otherwise handled correctly via the hook.
a11y: No interactive content. The debug HUD is fixed at z-50 with no role (715). Forced-colors and high-contrast are detected but only lower a score (538-541); there is no forced-colors styling.
api: Mutates global state: rewrites document.body.className with a regex and adds glass-tier-* (681-685), and sets ~13 CSS variables on :root (653-678) without restoring them on unmount. Two instances fight each other. EnhancedGlass accepts [key:string]:any (753). particles/webgl render empty placeholders (794-802).
ssr: 'use client', guarded by isBrowser(). The GPU probe reads WEBGL_debug_renderer_info UNMASKED_RENDERER (302-312), a fingerprinting vector that Firefox/Safari mask.
fake_complexity: Moderate. Capability scoring is a heuristic, which is acceptable, but the 'particle system would go here' placeholder (796) and the empty canvas (801) show unimplemented features. The FPS monitor downgrades one tier per second whenever fps<30 (577-590), so a busy tab cascades to 'minimal' and never recovers.
screenshot_review: Pixel stats: desktop mean 243, std 17, saturation 0. One grey card ('One material, gracefully enhanced') on white. The visible material is the story's class, not the component's.
target: Core quality-tier system (with GlassPerformanceOptimization and hooks/useGlassOptimization); keep only the capability-detection logic, drop EnhancedGlass
justification: This is the only tier implementation with real capability detection, so its detection logic is worth salvaging. As shipped, though, it is not exported, mutates body/root globally, auto-degrades permanently, and its main component carries a broken className. Fold the detection into the single core tier provider, scoped to a root element rather than document.body.

name: GlassQuantumStates

tests.nature: templated smoke/axe/className/snapshot; never clicks the button (which would crash)

material_impl: glass-surface-primary + glass-elev-2 utilities on the button (768-773), mixed with raw Tailwind 'relative overflow-hidden font-medium' and a runtime arbitrary class `duration-[${...}ms]` (771). Superposition stripes use the consumer-supplied color. Canvas fillStyle is set to a CSS 'color-mix(... var(--glass-white) ...)' string (887), which canvas cannot resolve, so it is silently ignored.
motion: framer-motion. Same reduced-motion bug as elsewhere: initial opacity 0 with animate={}, so stripes and the collapse overlay stay invisible (790-798, 817-818). The entanglement line keeps repeat:Infinity transitions even when animate={} (1042-1045).
a11y: GlassQuantumButton is a real <button>, but its label randomly changes after click (831) with no live region. Outcome is nondeterministic by design, which is an anti-pattern for a control. The interference canvas has no aria-hidden.
api: Non-functional as a system. (1) useReducedMotion() is called inside the click handler (752), a Rules-of-Hooks violation that throws 'Invalid hook call' on the first successful measurement. (2) The provider creates its system in useEffect (614-616), but child effects run first, so createQuantumState is a no-op (628) and the context 'system' is null and never re-rendered (674, 866), so the interference pattern never draws. (3) buttonId defaults to `quantum-button-${Date.now()}`, a new id every render (725). (4) The default render passes possibleStates=[] (1199), which divides by zero in normalize. (5) The context default object means the provider guard never throws (588-595, 690-698).
ssr: 'use client'. NodeJS.Timeout typing in browser code (305). One setInterval per created state is never cleared, evolving the matrix every ~75ms forever (374-386). cleanup() exists but is never called (617-619).
fake_complexity: Extreme. Complex numbers, a random 'Hermitian' Hamiltonian and Shannon-entropy 'coherence' are used to pick a random button label. Per-pixel fillRect on a 100x40 canvas every frame (883-890) for an effect that is invisible.
screenshot_review: Pixel stats: desktop mean 243, std 15, saturation 0. A grey card with a button on white. The certification marks hasCanvas=true, but the canvas never paints because system is null. The stripes use rgba(255,255,255,0.14-0.26) from the story, which is invisible on white.
justification: Pseudo-physics that randomises a button's meaning, crashes on click via a hook call inside an event handler, never initialises because of effect ordering, and leaks intervals. Only the useQuantumStates hook is root-exported, and it returns a no-op default context. There is nothing to salvage. Remove it together with the src/components/quantum family review.

name: GlassReactions
sub_exports: GlassReactionBar (not root; NAME COLLIDES with root-exported src/components/interactive/GlassReactionBar)
material_impl: Picker/bar use glass-surface-primary + glass-elev-2/3 (538, 660). Fallbacks are hard-coded 'bg-white shadow-lg' (539, 661). Emojis get 'glass-optimized-glass glass-blur-sm' (427), class names that exist in no stylesheet. The shimmer uses a triplicated 'glass-gradient-primary' class (468). The story supplies the actual glass surface via inline rgba and backdrop-filter (stories:15-25), so the component's own material is not what certification saw.
motion: Custom rAF gravity physics per emoji (383-421) plus framer enter/exit. The reduced-motion gating has the invisible-content bug: initial {opacity:0, scale:0} with animate={} leaves emojis and the picker invisible (436-449, 547-548, 664-665). 'age' is captured once at render (375), so the ageScale fade never progresses. The physics object from props is mutated (395).
a11y: The picker has role=menu/menuitem but no roving focus, arrow keys or focus move on open (555-583). Opening it requires a right-click (contextmenu hijack, 202-214); there is no keyboard path except global digit shortcuts. Those use a window 'keypress' listener that fires even while typing in any input on the page (281-302), a serious usability and a11y bug. Emoji buttons are labelled (571, 679). The hint is role=status with a static string (352).
api: No forwardRef. className and style are passed through. handleClick omits addReaction from its deps (198), a stale closure over props. children is required even though the overlay is the point. Raw Tailwind 'w-10 h-10 flex', 'hover:bg-white/10' and 'border-l-transparent' (563-564, 588-593) are only partly covered by storybook-utility-shim.
ssr: 'use client'. navigator.vibrate is called on every reaction (251-253); vibration without user opt-in is questionable.
fake_complexity: Low. It does what it says (floating emoji reactions), but double-click-to-burst with random emoji (174-189) is novelty behaviour.
screenshot_review: Pixel stats: desktop mean 240, std 17, saturation ~1. One big grey card with heading copy and a single tiny thumbs-up (intensity 0.1) in the corner. The surface is story-authored inline glass. The component's value (floating reactions and picker) is not visible in the certified frame.
target: One Reactions family (ReactionBar + ReactionPicker popover + optional floating burst overlay) merged with src/components/interactive/GlassReactionBar and src/components/social/GlassReactionBubbles
justification: A legitimate pattern with real, if crude, physics. It is undermined by a global digit-key hijack, right-click-only discovery, an inaccessible menu, and content that vanishes under reduced motion. Three reaction components exist with a name collision on GlassReactionBar. Merge them into one accessible family (popover with roving focus, scoped shortcuts, opacity-only reduced-motion variant).

name: GlassSelfHealingSystem
material_impl: The dashboard panel is bespoke inline glass: rgba(255,255,255,.30/.16/.18/.28), inset highlight, blur(24px) saturate(1.4) (1214-1223). It does not use createGlassStyle/OptimizedGlass. Status colours include a hard-coded '#7f1d1d' (92, 1132). The trigger uses raw Tailwind 'fixed top-4 left-4 z-50', 'w-12 h-12' and 'transition-all duration-300' (1283-1288).
motion: framer-motion. The dashboard and badges have the invisible-content-under-reduced-motion pattern (1225-1226, 1245-1246, 1306-1307).
a11y: The dashboard trigger has aria-label and aria-expanded (1290-1296), which is good. The portal panel has no role=dialog, no focus move and no Escape handling. The status dot conveys health by colour only, with the information in a title tooltip (1153-1159).
api: healingEnabled is accepted and unused (1058). components prop is unused (1361). The context default is non-null, so the guard never throws (955-969, 1042-1050). The diagnostic MutationObserver watches childList+attributes+subtree (1108-1118), and the component itself writes data-* attributes on each diagnosis (1144-1147), creating self-triggered re-diagnosis churn (throttled to 3s).
ssr: 'use client'. The VisualAnomalyDetector constructor calls document.createElement, but only from the effect-created system (989).
fake_complexity: Severe. Every 'healing' action is a setTimeout that resolves true and changes nothing (860-929). The 'computer vision' snapshot is a solid colour derived from a style-string hash (125-137); the serialised blob is created and discarded (120-122). Infinite async recursion: diagnoseComponent→initiateHealing→diagnoseComponent, and because the re-diagnosis overwrites status 'healing', any persistent critical issue (e.g. contrast<3 on translucent glass, since parseColor ignores alpha at 449-457) loops forever (774-776, 798-803, 843-847). Any page above 50MB heap is flagged a 'memory-leak' (619-635).
screenshot_review: Pixel stats: desktop mean 244, std 12, saturation 0. A single grey card ('Workspace surface healthy') on white. The certified story is the provider story, so the dashboard is not in the certified frame.
target: Dev-only diagnostics in src/tools/GlassDevTools (axe + real contrast checks), not a runtime component
justification: Claims automatic visual and a11y repair but every fix is a no-op timer, and the diagnosis can recurse forever while burning a MutationObserver per wrapper in production. Runtime 'self-healing' is the wrong abstraction for a design system. Correctness belongs in build-time lint, tests and devtools.

name: GlassSpatialAudio
material_impl: The visualizer uses glass-surface-primary/subtle utilities (828, 841). GlassAudioReactive animates a hard-coded rgba(255,255,255,0.1+) background (788). Source dots fall back to hard-coded '#ec4899' (897, 928). Grid lines are positioned through ref callbacks mutating style (848-850, 857-859) instead of style props. The legend's colour swatches (green 'Listener', emerald/amber/pink classes, 954-971) do not match the rendered dot colours (glass-surface-primary listener, hsl tokens).
motion: framer-motion. The source pulse rings respect reduced motion. GlassAudioReactive's analysis rAF loop is never cancelled (749-764) and calls setState every frame.
a11y: Audio is not autoplayed: it initialises on first click, keydown or touch (587-605), which is correct. There is no UI to mute, nor a 'sounds enabled' control. The visualizer is decorative with no role/aria-hidden. GlassSpatialAudio renders only an sr-only string by default (682-686), so screen readers announce 'Glass spatial audio provider active', which is noise.
api: Critical bug: the provider effect depends on [autoInitialize, isInitialized, settings] (619). After the first interaction sets isInitialized=true, the effect re-runs and replaces engineRef with a NEW uninitialised engine (585), so playSound returns early (404) and sounds never play after initialisation. An object-literal settings prop also re-creates the engine on every parent render. The autoInitialize branch's cleanup never calls engine.cleanup(), leaking an AudioContext (607-611).
ssr: 'use client'. Window access is confined to effects. GLASS_SOUNDS embeds truncated, unused base64 WAV data URLs (93-129) as dead bundle weight.
fake_complexity: Partial. The HRTF PannerNode graph is real Web Audio (351-373) and the synthetic 'glass' tones are real (267-324). The 'spatial' positions, however, map screen x/y onto a 2D plane at z=0 (1046-1057), so HRTF adds little beyond stereo panning.
screenshot_review: Pixel stats: desktop mean 244, std 12, saturation 0. One grey informational card. The component itself renders nothing visible; the visual is story copy.
target: Single opt-in non-visual audio-feedback service (useGlassSound) merged with src/utils/soundDesign, shipped from a subpath, default off
justification: The only file in this shard with a genuine browser-API implementation. A provider-effect bug, though, guarantees no sound plays once initialised, AudioContexts leak, and the visual exports (visualizer, audio-reactive) are debug toys. Keep one small, opt-in sound service with a mute/consent API and drop the visual components.

name: GlassTrophyCase
material_impl: Mostly utility classes, many of which do not exist: 'glass-text-primary-glass-opacity-60' and 'glass-text-primary-opacity-50' are caught by a [class*=...] selector that forces full text colour with !important (src/styles/glass.css:1915-1918), so all intended opacity hierarchy collapses. Tier colours are neutral grey tokens for all five tiers (71-100), so bronze, gold and diamond look the same. Hex-alpha suffixes are appended to CSS var() strings (`${tierColor.primary}20` → 'var(--glass-border-default)20', 519-520, 567, 874, 891-892), producing invalid declarations that are dropped. Per-achievement glowColor hex values are defined but never used (128-284). 'glass-surface-dark/50' backdrop (851).
motion: framer-motion with initial={false} under reduced motion (510), the correct pattern unlike siblings. The infinite glow pulse is gated (535-547). whileHover/whileTap scale are not gated (507-508, 788-789).
a11y: Achievement cards are clickable motion.divs with no role, tabIndex or key handler (495-514), so the detail view is mouse-only. The detail 'modal' has no role=dialog, aria-modal, focus trap, Escape or close button (847-977). Headings are faked with role=heading on divs (583-593). Search and selects are labelled (717, 730, 748, 766). The show-locked toggle lacks aria-pressed (809-827).
api: No forwardRef, no style passthrough, className concatenated by string template. AchievementCard is declared inside render (489), so it remounts on every state change, breaking layout animation and focus. Typed props are then cast to any in filters (318, 387). Search bypasses the secret filter and leaks secret achievements (338-349). 'list' view renders identical cards (832-836). userStats is unused (293).
ssr: 'use client'. A new AudioContext is created per unlock and never closed (437-438). The unlock effect re-fires for all eligible achievements whenever the achievements reference changes (472-487).
fake_complexity: Low: a straightforward gallery. The default data is reading-app specific ('Read 50 articles').
duplicates: src/components/modal/GlassModal.tsx (should be used for the detail view)
screenshot_review: Pixel stats: desktop mean 249, std 20, saturation 0, only 2.5% of pixels differ from the white background. Almost entirely blank white with faint grey outlines, so the case reads as empty. Mobile is 6.4% content. Also listed in reports/strict-mobile-component-defects (trophy-*.png), indicating known mobile defects.
target: src/components/advanced/GlassAchievementSystem (rebuild on GlassCard + GlassModal + GlassBadge with real tier tokens)
justification: A plausible product pattern, but tier identity is erased (all greys), colour-alpha math produces invalid CSS, opacity classes are flattened by a global attribute selector, and cards plus the modal are not keyboard-accessible. It duplicates the root-exported GlassAchievementSystem and is not itself exported. Merge into one achievement gallery composed from existing primitives.

name: GlassWebGLShader
material_impl: Real WebGL fragment shaders (66-259), but they sample a synthetic 256x256 red/green gradient texture (455-487), not the page backdrop. This is a coloured gradient effect, not glass. The CSS fallback mixes createGlassStyle with hard-coded rgba borders, gradients and shadows (31-51). It references class 'ag-webgl-shader-orb' (553), which exists in no stylesheet.
motion: Continuous rAF when animated. Respects reduced motion via shouldAnimate (284-285) and disables the mouse listener (369). The fallback animations are explicitly undefined.
a11y: The canvas is aria-hidden (602). The CSS fallback is role=status and announces 'CSS shader … Lightweight preview mode active' (534, 568-586), debug copy that is wrong in production.
api: No forwardRef. The style prop is merged. The canvas is fixed at width=800/height=600 with no resize observer or DPR (600-601), so it is blurry and distorted at other sizes. Without compact/contained/preview or an explicit height, the wrapper's only child is position:absolute, so it collapses to 0 height. u_mouse is not y-flipped. Changing intensity tears down and recreates the GL context (365).
ssr: 'use client'. Context access is in an effect. Lose-context on cleanup is good.
fake_complexity: Moderate. 'frosted' and 'prism' use `int samples = N; for (int i = 0; i < samples; i++)` (153-155, 236-238), a non-constant loop bound that GLSL ES 1.00 (WebGL1 Appendix A, enforced by ANGLE) rejects. Those variants fail to compile and silently fall to the CSS fallback. The certified 'prism' story's DOM text confirms fallback: 'CSS shader prism glass field Lightweight preview mode active' (reports/glassmorphism-storybook-visual-certification.json, GlassWebGLShader inspection, hasCanvas=false), yet the entry is 'passed'.
screenshot_review: Pixel stats: desktop mean 245, std 13, saturation 0 for a component named 'prism'/'dispersion'. The frame is a grey CSS fallback panel overlaid by the story's own inline glass card ('Prism Refraction Preview'). No shader output is visible.
target: One WebGL effect primitive (with LiquidGlassGPU) under an /effects or /three subpath; fix GLSL const loops, resize/DPR, sample a real backdrop or rename to a gradient shader
justification: The only real shader code in the library, but two of its five variants cannot compile on spec-conformant WebGL, it never refracts actual content, and the certified screenshot is its fallback panel with debug copy. It duplicates LiquidGlassGPU's goal. Merge into one well-engineered shader surface, or demote to a decorative 'GlassShaderBackground'.
evidence: reports/glassmorphism-storybook-visual-certification.json (GlassWebGLShader inspections: hasCanvas false, bodyText 'CSS shader prism glass field')

name: IntelligentColorSystem
sub_exports: useIntelligentColor. None root-exported, but transitively public via root-exported BrandColorIntegration (src/components/advanced/BrandColorIntegration.tsx:16, 57)
material_impl: The demo surface is an inline gradient of palette glassBase/glassTint (754-756) plus utility 'glass-blur-backdrop'. Palette defaults hard-code hex fallbacks (#8b5cf6, #06b6d4, #0f172a…) (61-89).
motion: framer-motion with initial={false} under reduced motion (758), which is correct. The toggle knob animate={} under reduced motion means the switch knob never moves (933-935), so the state is not shown.
a11y: The 'Auto-adaptation' toggle is a button without role=switch or aria-checked (915-942). Labels are <label> elements not associated with any control (807-815, 841-848, 912-914). Swatch buttons are labelled 'Apply brand color N' only. ContrastGuard is wrapped around plain text (791-798, 833).
api: Global side effects. On mount the provider writes --glass-text-primary/-secondary/-tertiary/-disabled, --glass-bg-default, --glass-border-default/-subtle and --glass-gradient-default onto document.documentElement and never restores them (654-705), so mounting one demo reskins the entire app. In dark mode it assigns 'var(--glass-text-primary)' to --glass-text-primary itself (83, 665), a cyclic custom property that becomes guaranteed-invalid and breaks all text colour. Time-of-day and season shifts are ON by default (276-279, 622-651), so colours change by clock and calendar (non-deterministic UI). The colour math accepts only #hex, while every palette value is a CSS var()/hsl(var()) string, so adaptToBrand, adaptToPalette and contrast adjustment are no-ops for the built-in values (107-123, 236-237, 487); the demo's own brand swatches pass hsl(var()) and are ignored (739-744, 897). Reading document in the useState initialiser causes a hydration mismatch (264-271).
ssr: 'use client'. document is read during render (264-267), so server and client initial state diverge.
fake_complexity: High. 'Intelligent' analysis reads two computed colours (297-301). 'Mood' is two thresholds (350-358). Seasonal and time palettes are hard-coded switches.
screenshot_review: Pixel stats: desktop mean 242, std 12, saturation 0. The palette swatch grid is effectively grey because the story forces #737373. Mobile has saturation 4 and 78% content: a dense grid of swatches and small buttons. Utilitarian demo, not premium.
target: Brand/accent API in src/theme/ThemeProvider (scoped CSS vars on a theme root, OKLCH-based accessible ramps); rebuild BrandColorIntegration on it
justification: A provider that silently overwrites core text and background tokens on :root, creates a cyclic --glass-text-primary in dark mode, and shifts colours by time and season is a correctness hazard for every consumer. Its adaptive math cannot parse its own palette values. Theming must be deterministic and scoped, so remove this and move brand-colour input into the ThemeProvider.

name: LiquidGlassGPU
material_impl: Always renders its CSS fallback: hard-coded rgba gradient, border and blur(24px) saturate(1.5) (789-793), not tokens or OptimizedGlass. Imports LIQUID_GLASS tokens for ior/thickness/sheen defaults (628-630), but material/variant props are ignored.
motion: A rAF render loop (699-754) is restarted on every deviceTilt change. useReducedMotion is imported but never used (25). The deviceorientation listener has no iOS permission request.
api: The GPU path is unreachable. isGPUSupported starts false (642), so the first render is the fallback branch, which contains no <canvas> (778-799). The init effect returns early because canvasRef.current is null (651) and never re-runs (deps [onFallback]). The certification inspection confirms hasCanvas=false. Even if reached, uProjection/uModelView are never set (34-42, 503-567), so gl_Position is the zero vector and nothing would draw. No forwardRef, no style prop.
ssr: 'use client'. Self-labelled '@demo DEMO / SHOWCASE COMPONENT… metrics… simulated' (2-9), yet exported from the root as a product component.
fake_complexity: Severe. The 'backdrop capture' paints a hard-coded indigo→violet→pink gradient (586-598), with the comment 'For now, create a simple placeholder' (573-578). Fresnel/IOR shader code is decorative because it never executes.
screenshot_review: Pixel stats: desktop mean 243, std 18, saturation 1. A grey rounded panel (CSS fallback) beside a story-authored stat sidebar. The certified bodyText begins with the story's raw <style> CSS text, showing the inspector read style text as content. No GPU effect is visible.
target: OptimizedGlass / a single Liquid Glass material primitive (CSS + optional SVG-filter refraction); any real WebGL path merges into the consolidated shader primitive with GlassWebGLShader
justification: Named after the library's core promise ('Liquid Glass'), but structurally it can never reach its GPU path and always shows a hard-coded CSS fallback. Its own header admits it is a demo. Shipping it from the root misleads users about what the material system is. Deprecate it with an alias to the real material primitive and remove it in 5.x.

name: LivingEcosystemSimulator
material_impl: Uses the shared OptimizedGlass primitive (129-137), the healthiest pattern in this shard. It is mixed with raw Tailwind that aura-glass does not ship ('bg-gradient-to-br from-white/10 via-white/5 to-white/8' at 134, 'text-red-400' at 171, 'focus-visible:ring-cyan-400' at 189, arbitrary 'shadow-[0_0_30px_-10px_rgba(248,113,113,0.7)]' at 192, 'bg-red-400/80'/'bg-cyan-400/80' at 228, 'text-emerald-300' at 249). src/styles/storybook-utility-shim.css covers only some of these (bg-red-400 yes; bg-gradient-to-br, from-white, text-red-400, focus-visible:ring absent), so consumers get partial styling. statusAccent uses 'glass-surface-green/40 border-green-400/40' (67-70).
motion: None beyond a CSS transition-all. No reduced-motion concerns.
a11y: region with aria-label (130-131). Layer cards are real buttons, but each contains h3/p/div (184-259), which violates the button content model (phrasing only). Status is carried by both text label and colour, which is good. Focus ring via an unshimmed Tailwind class plus glass-focus.
api: Clean props (layers, onSelectLayer, highlightThreshold, title). className passthrough; no forwardRef or style passthrough. The selected state is not tracked or exposed (no aria-pressed).
fake_complexity: The name says 'Simulator' and the copy says 'Real-time biosphere telemetry' (144), but nothing is simulated. It is a static 4-card stat dashboard over props.
screenshot_review: No certification screenshot exists for this component.
target: examples/ recipe (domain dashboard composed from GlassCard + GlassProgress + GlassBadge)
justification: Honest, small and built on the right primitive, but it is domain-specific demo content (habitats, biodiversity) with a misleading 'simulator / real-time' name, and it depends on Tailwind utilities the package does not ship. It belongs in examples as a composition recipe, not in the public component API.

name: MolecularBondingInterface
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shell (86-94). Bond rows rely on raw Tailwind gradient classes ('bg-gradient-to-r from-purple-500/70 to-fuchsia-500/40' etc., 64-69, 168-171; 'rounded-2xl border border-white/10 px-4 py-3' at 168) that the package does not ship, so in consumer apps without Tailwind the bond colour coding (the only 'bonding' visual) likely does not render. Fallback 'from-slate-500/60 to-slate-700/30' (161).
a11y: group with label. Bond rows are buttons. In the molecule list a <div> sits inside a <span> (120-127), which is invalid. The '⇄' glyph is read aloud (179-180). Charge is colour plus sign, which is acceptable.
api: Simple props (molecules, bonds, onInspectBond); no forwardRef or style. Bonds referencing missing nodes silently disappear (157).
fake_complexity: 'Visualize complex bonding interactions' (100-101), but there is no graph, geometry or visualization. It is two lists.
screenshot_review: No certification screenshot exists for this component.
justification: A chemistry-themed list pair with no actual bonding visualization, whose only colour coding depends on Tailwind classes the library does not provide. It has no reusable value as a design-system component.

name: MultiDimensionalGestureRecognizer
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shell (103-111) with raw Tailwind 'bg-gradient-to-br from-white/10 via-indigo-500/15 to-white/5' (108) and card classes 'rounded-2xl border border-white/10 bg-white/5 p-4' plus an arbitrary rgba shadow (137-141), only partly shimmed.
motion: None. useReducedMotion is used to hide the 'N axes' count text (181-185), which is semantically meaningless.
a11y: role='application' on the whole region (104) switches screen readers out of browse mode for what is a set of plain buttons, a misuse. Buttons contain h3, dl and ul (132-204), an invalid content model. The active gesture is not exposed (no aria-pressed).
api: Props: gestures, onRecognize, showConfidence. No forwardRef or style.
fake_complexity: Total. There are no pointer, touch, device-motion or pressure listeners anywhere. 'Recognize' means clicking a card (94-100, 132-135). The 'six-axis motion patterns' copy (117-118) is fiction.
screenshot_review: No certification screenshot exists for this component.
justification: Named a gesture recognizer, but it recognises nothing: it is three clickable description cards with an ARIA 'application' role that harms screen-reader users. A real gesture primitive (if needed) should be a headless hook (usePointerGesture) next to GlassGestureZone.

name: StorybookVisualShowcase
material_impl: Fully bespoke: an inline <style> string with hard-coded hex text colours (#0f172a, #0f766e, #334155), rgba fills and blur(24px) saturate(1.8) (145-416). No tokens, no primitives, and it shares nothing with the library's material system.
a11y: Renders an <h1> (77) inside whatever page hosts it; status pills are plain spans.
api: name/kind/summary only. Not exported, and no file imports it (rg across src/stories finds zero consumers).
fake_complexity: Integrity risk. It renders canned 'audit' claims regardless of the component named: 'Reduced motion', 'Contrast AA', 'No overlap or clipping', 'Clear liquid material', plus fake metrics 'Latency 18 ms', 'Clarity 94' (25-56, 117-122). Git history: commit dd9c1f5b8 'Prepare AuraGlass 3.0 release QA' added 74 story lines referencing it, i.e. stories were replaced by this surrogate scene so certification screenshots showed canned copy instead of the component. Those usages were later removed and the file is now orphaned. reports/audit/triage.md:226 already flags it as 'demo copy'.
screenshot_review: No current screenshot. Historically it was the content of many certification screenshots (see git history).
justification: Dead code whose only historical purpose was to stand in for real components in visual certification with pre-written 'AA / no clipping / reduced motion' claims. Delete it, and add a CI guard that fails if a story renders a surrogate rather than its declared component.
evidence: git show dd9c1f5b8 (74 added lines referencing StorybookVisualShowcase)
